chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The one in Ihram should withhold his nose from the pleasant scent, and he should not withhold his nose from the foul smell.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: The person in the state of Ihram (ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: What are the rules for a person in Ihram regarding smelling perfumes and bad odors?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic distinction between 'benefit' (istif'ah) and 'removal of harm' (daf' al-darar) in the state of Ihram. While Imam al-Sadiq (AS) prohibits blocking pleasant scents to preserve the state of spiritual detachment, he permits blocking foul odors as a natural physiological response, demonstrating that Ihram restrictions are specific to luxury rather than basic comfort.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Hammad, from Al Halby, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one in Ihraam should withhold his nose from the aromas of perfumes, and he should not withhold his nose from the fetid smells’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from Hammad from al-Halabiy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One in the state of Ihram must hold his nose from sweet smelling things, but not from bad smelling ones.’”
